summary: Owned units s0067–s0088 are Wang Xizhi’s Kuaiji-period counsel: a letter to the Prince of Kuaiji about Yin Hao’s northern deployments, then famine relief and a letter headed 尚書僕射謝安. No owned unit states a birth, death, age, or reign-year for p025, p026, p027, or p030. Claims 195 and 199 convert the letter’s deictic 今/當今 into a closed AD 353–354 interval; Jinshu 8 places Hao and Xun Xian in the field from Yonghe 8 (conventional AD 352) and strips Hao only in Yonghe 10/II (AD 354), so both endpoints are unargued and the window reads like campaign activity rather than uncertainty about one letter. Claims 204 and 242, and the matching active hints, treat 伍員之憂不獨在昔 and 蹈東海 as explicit Spring-and-Autumn / Warring-States life dates (BC 522–484; BC 284–260). The Chinese marks those passages as ancient exempla inside an Eastern Jin letter; the imported years are not in the source, 522 is Wu Yuan’s Zuozhuan flight rather than a birth, and 284–260 does not match Lu Zhonglian’s Handan 蹈東海 speech after Changping. Claim 215 dates 時東土饑荒 to AD 353–355 without a source year, using a tenure-like span. Claim 236 dates Xie An’s receipt of a puye letter to AD 353–355, which the same chapter contradicts (謝安未仕時亦居焉) and which Jinshu 8–79 assign to Xie Shang in Yonghe, not to Xie An. All ten owned items and all four owned people therefore fail; later reception must stay a retrospective event and must not feed active hints.

itemChecks.event: Yin Hao is named as the general who should be pulled back to Hefei while Jin armies still stand at Xuchang, Qiao, Liang, and Pengcheng.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of the dated event is Yin Hao, but only as the living addressee of a recall in Wang Xizhi’s letter to the Prince of Kuaiji, not as the subject of a year-dated campaign entry. The source date is the letter’s 今/當今 (s0069, s0074), which is deictic present, not 永和九年/十年. A Western closed interval must justify each endpoint against that one speech-act. Jinshu 8 has Hao already moving on Xuchang–Sikou in Yonghe 8 (conventional AD 352) with Xun Xian at Huaiyin, defeated at Shansang in Yonghe 9/X (AD 353), and dismissed only in Yonghe 10/II (AD 354). Start-year 353 therefore drops the first documented field year that matches 西輸許洛 and 許昌諸軍; end-year 354 is the dismissal year, not a demonstrated letter date. Competing placements (after Xie Shang’s Yonghe 8 defeat when Hao 復圖再舉, or during/after the Yonghe 9 advance) remain open. Certainty explicit-event-contextual-date overstates a guessed two-ended span. Conventional Yonghe-year labels are used here as year-only equivalents (Yonghe 8=352, 9=353, 10=354); no month/day in the letter requires a proleptic-Gregorian conversion.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵，許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城諸軍皆還保淮
此實當今策之上者
今功未可期，而遺黎殲盡，萬不餘一
況今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河

itemChecks.event: Xun Xian is named in the same recall as the general who should return to hold Guangling.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Xun Xian, again only as a commander named in Wang Xizhi’s present-tense advice, not as the subject of an annalistic year. The claim copies the same 今 → AD 353–354 conversion as claim-195. Jinshu 8 stations 北中郎荀羨 at Huaiyin in Yonghe 8/III and treats him as Hao’s colleague through the northern push; nothing in s0074 pins his withdrawal-order to 353 rather than 352, or keeps him in the field through 354. Endpoints are therefore unearned, and the interval must not be read as Xun Xian’s activity across two years.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵，許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城諸軍皆還保淮
此實當今策之上者

itemChecks.event: The letter only recalls Wu Zixu’s ancient warning as an exemplum; it does not date Wu Zixu’s own Spring and Autumn career.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of any dated life event cannot be Wu Zixu here. 常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔 explicitly contrasts antiquity (在昔) with the Eastern Jin present and pairs it with 麋鹿之游, the later-attested Gusu-terrace warning. That is retrospective-reference / reception, not Wu Zixu’s own dated act. Certainty explicit is false: s0081 gives no year. BC 522–484 is imported. Zuozhuan Zhao 20 (conventional BC 522) is Wu Yuan’s flight after Wu She is killed, not a birth; Shiji/Zuozhuan place his death in 魯哀公十一年 / Fuchai 11 (conventional BC 484), after the Ai-ling campaign. Even those external years would date other events, and the 麋鹿 warning belongs to the Fuchai years, not a 38-year activity window. Do not feed this reception into life dates or active hints.

evidence.quote: 常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔，麋鹿之游將不止林藪而已

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi opened the granaries during an eastern famine and pressed the court to ease Wu–Kuaiji levies.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xizhi; 開倉振貸 and the memorials are his own acts. The only source time-word is 時, which situates the famine in his Kuaiji service after the Hao letter, not in named years. AD 353–355 looks like a tenure span from the later Lan-ting Yonghe 9 notice to the Yonghe 11/III resignation oath elsewhere in the same biography, which is activity-through-office, not uncertainty about one famine. Start-year 353 is not in s0083–s0085. Yonghe 11 can supply an onOrBefore bound for acts as 會稽內史, but a second endpoint must not be invented, and 時 remains unresolved as a calendar year. Certainty explicit-event-contextual-date is too strong for a yearless 時.

evidence.quote: 時東土饑荒，羲之輒開倉振貸
羲之每上疏爭之，事多見從

itemChecks.event: A letter on Kuaiji administration is addressed to Xie An under the title Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
itemChecks.reason: Owner, if the heading is taken literally, is Xie An as the puye correspondent. Dating that receipt to AD 353–355 is impossible on the same book: this chapter later says 謝安未仕時亦居焉 during the Kuaiji/Lan-ting years, and Jinshu 79 has him refuse office until after Xie Wan’s fall, already past forty, with 尚書僕射 only then. Jinshu 8 instead makes 謝尚 puye in Yonghe 9/IV (AD 353), which fits the letter’s Kuaiji administrative present (s0086–s0088 今事之大者未布，漕運是也) but is a different person. The extracted 353–355 interval therefore dates Xie An by a title he did not then hold. Preserve the heading as an anachronistic or textually disputed address; do not turn it into Xie An’s living activity in 353–355, and do not use the heading as a life date.

evidence.quote: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：
頃所陳論，每蒙允納，所以令下小得蘇息，各安其業
今事之大者未布，漕運是也

itemChecks.event: The Kuaiji letter uses Lu Zhonglian’s jump-into-the-Eastern-Sea resolve only as a proverb for mass flight, not as Lu Zhonglian’s own dated act.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of a Warring-States life date cannot be Lu Zhonglian in s0087. 此一郡久以蹈東海矣 is Wang Xizhi’s counterfactual about his commandery, a reception of the Shiji/Zhanguoce line 則連有蹈東海而死耳 spoken during the Handan siege in 趙孝成王時 after Changping. Certainty explicit is false; BC 284–260 is not in the Chinese. Zhao Xiaocheng’s reign is BC 265–245; Changping is Qin Zhaoxiang 46 / BC 260; the speech belongs to the later siege (often placed in Zhao Xiaocheng 8 / BC 258), not to a 284–260 activity band. Keep the allusion as retrospective reception dated with the letter, not as Lu’s living years.

evidence.quote: 若不耳，此一郡久以蹈東海矣

itemChecks.event: The hint restates Yin Hao’s recommended Hefei withdrawal as if AD 353–354 were established active years.
itemChecks.reason: Active hints must track a supported personal event. The only owned event is the undated 今 recall in s0074. AD 353–354 therefore repeats the unjustified closed interval of claim-195 and looks like multi-year campaign activity. Until the letter is given unresolved or one-sided Yonghe 8–early 10 bounds, the hint cannot stand.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵

itemChecks.event: The hint restates Xun Xian’s recommended Guangling withdrawal as if AD 353–354 were established active years.
itemChecks.reason: Same defect as hints-p025: the hint is not backed by a year in s0074 and should not imply Xun Xian was active throughout 353–354 on the strength of one 今.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵

itemChecks.event: The hint lacks a personal dated event of Wu Zixu; the chapter only cites 伍員之憂 as an ancient exemplum.
itemChecks.reason: Reception must not feed active-date hints. BC 522–484 is not Wu Zixu living activity attested by s0081, and 522 is not even a birth in the external annals. Clear the hint or replace it only if a separately supported life event exists, which these units do not provide.

evidence.quote: 常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔

itemChecks.event: The hint lacks a personal dated event of Lu Zhonglian; the chapter only uses 蹈東海 proverbially.
itemChecks.reason: BC 284–260 is an invented activity window built from a retrospective proverb. It must not appear as Lu Zhonglian’s active dates.

evidence.quote: 此一郡久以蹈東海矣

personChecks.reason: Yin Hao appears only in s0074 as a general to be seated at Hefei. Owned units omit no birth, death, or age that the narrative actually states; they simply give none. The supplied chronology is the AD 353–354 attestation plus matching hint. That isolates one undated 今 and converts it into a two-year activity band, ignoring Jinshu 8’s Yonghe 8–10 sequence and the letter’s single-moment character. Do not certify p025 from this isolated, mis-converted event.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵

personChecks.reason: Xun Xian is likewise named only in the s0074 pair. No life dates exist in the owned units to extract. The AD 353–354 hint copies claim-199’s unsupported interval and cannot be read as his career window. Same-chapter context does not add a year for him inside s0067–s0088.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵

personChecks.reason: Wu Zixu’s only owned appearance is the s0081 allusion. Treating BC 522–484 as his chronology contradicts 不獨在昔 and imports years the chapter does not give. There is no omitted birth/death clause in these units; the defect is a reception misread as living activity. A later biography may still attest earlier events, but this letter attests only the reception.

evidence.quote: 常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔，麋鹿之游將不止林藪而已

personChecks.reason: Lu Zhonglian is present only as the 蹈東海 proverb in s0087. BC 284–260 is not a source date and does not match the Handan speech. Person-level chronology is therefore incoherent: a retrospective figure has been given active Warring-States years from an Eastern Jin administrative letter.

evidence.quote: 若不耳，此一郡久以蹈東海矣

findings.problem: s0074’s 今/當今 dates one Kuaiji letter naming Yin Hao and Xun Xian; the closed AD 353–354 interval drops Yonghe 8 (AD 352) when both were already in the northern deployment and treats Yonghe 10 (AD 354, Hao’s dismissal) as a safe end, turning a single present into two-year activity.
findings.action: Keep the rows as contemporary attestations of Hao and Xun Xian in the recall. Replace westernInterval 353–354 with unresolved:true and a reason that the letter has no reign year, or with westernBounds onOrAfter AD 352 and onOrBefore AD 354 that preserve the Yonghe 8 / 9 / early-10 competing placements. Do not invent a second exact year. Synchronize hints-p025 and hints-p026 to that repaired uncertainty; do not leave AD 353–354 as active hints.

findings.problem: 伍員之憂不獨在昔 is Wang Xizhi’s retrospective exemplum, yet claim-204 and the p027 hint date Wu Zixu’s own life to BC 522–484 with certainty explicit.
findings.action: Reclassify the Wu Zixu mention as retrospective-reference or receptionType retrospective, dated with the Kuaiji letter (same unresolved/bounded present as claims 195/199), not with Spring-and-Autumn years. Remove BC 522–484 from the attestation and from active hints. Do not add a birth or death from Zuozhuan Zhao 20 / Ai 11; those are other events and are not what s0081 attests.

findings.problem: 蹈東海 in s0087 is a proverbial reception of Lu Zhonglian’s Handan speech, yet the claim assigns explicit BC 284–260 life years and the hint repeats them.
findings.action: Keep the allusion as retrospective reception at the letter’s present. Delete BC 284–260 from the claim and from hints-p030. Do not substitute Changping/Handan years (BC 260/258) as Lu’s life dates in this chapter.

findings.problem: 時東土饑荒 names Wang Xizhi’s granary relief without a year; AD 353–355 is a tenure-like span, not a justified uncertainty window for that famine.
findings.action: Keep subject/predicate (Wang Xizhi’s relief/attestation). Mark the source date 時 unresolved, or use westernBounds only where the same biography actually bounds Kuaiji office (onOrBefore the Yonghe 11/III resignation). Do not keep start-year 353 merely because Lan-ting is Yonghe 9.

findings.problem: Dating Xie An as 尚書僕射 correspondent in AD 353–355 contradicts this chapter’s 謝安未仕時亦居焉 and Jinshu 79; Yonghe puye belongs to Xie Shang in Jinshu 8.
findings.action: Do not assign AD 353–355 as Xie An’s activity. Leave names untouched. Treat the puye heading as anachronistic or contested labeling: if Xie An remains the subject, record retrospective/anachronistic title and drop the Yonghe living interval; do not silently retitle the addressee. The letter body (漕運, 此一郡) stays a Kuaiji-period administrative text for Wang Xizhi, not an active date for Xie An.

references.quote: 中軍將軍殷浩帥衆北伐，次泗口
references.reason: Primary annal placing Yin Hao’s first northern move, with Xun Xian already at Huaiyin, in Yonghe 8 rather than 353.

references.quote: 冬十月，中軍將軍殷浩進次山桑，使平北將軍姚襄爲前鋒，襄叛，反擊浩，浩棄輜重，退保譙城。
references.reason: Primary annal for the Yonghe 9 Shansang defeat that competes with a 352 letter date and does not by itself lock 353–354.

references.quote: 廢揚州刺史殷浩爲庶人

references.title: 晉書/卷080 王羲之傳
references.reason: Same-chapter witness that Xie An was still out of office in the Kuaiji years that contain the puye letter heading.
